hints: Follow the carbon atoms all the way through, from X to the hydrocarbon to the CO2, since every C in the CO2 must have come from X.
Start at the end by working out moles of CO2 from 108 cm3 at r.t.p. using moles = volume / 24000, this tells you moles of C atoms.
For a formula Al_aC_b, moles of C = b x moles of X, so set b x 0.216 / (27a + 12b) equal to your moles of C and find which Al to C ratio fits.
walkthrough:
**Find moles of carbon from the CO2**

All the carbon in X ends up in the hydrocarbon and then in CO2. So moles of C in X equals moles of CO2 made.

Chemical calculation rule:
$$ \text{moles} = \frac{\text{volume in cm}^3}{24000} $$
$$ n(\text{CO}_2) = \frac{108}{24000} = 0.0045 \text{ mol} $$
So there are 0.0045 mol of C atoms in the 0.216 g sample.

**Link moles of X to moles of C**

Let the formula be $\text{Al}_a\text{C}_b$. One mole of X contains b moles of C atoms.

Chemical calculation rule:
$$ n(\text{X}) = \frac{0.216}{27a + 12b} $$
$$ n(\text{C}) = b \times n(\text{X}) = \frac{0.216b}{27a + 12b} = 0.0045 $$

**Solve for the Al to C ratio**

Rearrange to find the ratio a to b.
$$ 0.216b = 0.0045(27a + 12b) $$
$$ 0.216b = 0.1215a + 0.054b $$
$$ 0.162b = 0.1215a $$
$$ \frac{a}{b} = \frac{0.162}{0.1215} = 1.33 = \frac{4}{3} $$
So a : b = 4 : 3, giving $\text{Al}_4\text{C}_3$. A quick check: $M_r = 4(27) + 3(12) = 144$, $n = 0.216/144 = 0.0015$ mol, and $3 \times 0.0015 = 0.0045$ mol C, which matches perfectly.

options.A: Al2C3 has Mr = 90. 0.216 g would be 0.0024 mol, giving 3 x 0.0024 = 0.0072 mol C, which would make 172.8 cm3 CO2, far too much. It reverses the correct 4:3 ratio.
options.B: Al3C2 has Mr = 105. 0.216 g would be about 0.00206 mol, giving 2 x 0.00206 = 0.00411 mol C, which would make about 98.7 cm3 CO2, too little. The Al to C ratio is too high.
options.C: Al3C4 has Mr = 129. 0.216 g would be about 0.00167 mol, giving 4 x 0.00167 = 0.00670 mol C, which would make about 160.7 cm3 CO2, too much. It has too much carbon per aluminium.
options.D: Al4C3 has Mr = 144. 0.216 g is 0.0015 mol, which contains 3 x 0.0015 = 0.0045 mol C. This burns to give 0.0045 x 24000 = 108 cm3 CO2, exactly matching the data. This is aluminium carbide, which hydrolyses to methane.
